title: Bug: Dockerfile has no multi-stage web/worker targets — smoke would fail at build step
description:
Dockerfile is a single-stage image with no AS targets. .github/workflows/aws-fargate.yml lines 127 + 139 build with --target web and --target worker which would fail with 'failed to find stage' immediately. Same problem for any local Path B build script.

Also has stale content from main: line 32 references 'helm/connect-manager pre-install hook' (kubernetes-era), lines 37-41 set up DATA_DIR for SQLite, lines 42-43 hardcode VALKEY_HOST/PORT (works for local docker-compose but in prod we get VALKEY_URL from Secrets Manager — see awsk-m2n).

Fix: convert to multi-stage with shared base + 'web' (uvicorn) and 'worker' (arq) targets. Drop SQLite/keyring/helm crud. Use uv for dep management to match the rest of the project (pyproject.toml + uv.lock). Migrate task reuses web image with command override (already what the migrate workflow job does).

title: Bug: UserSession.save_datastore_for_browsing + remove_datastore_credentials are no-ops (legacy shim)
description:
main.py:568 calls state.save_datastore_for_browsing() to persist DataStore S3 credentials. The UserSession method calls _legacy_save_datastore_credentials, which is the awsk-opc shim that warns and returns None. Net effect: every credential entered through the modal is silently discarded — user gets a 'success' UI response, refreshes, credentials are gone, and the worker can't import because there's no DB row.

Same bug in remove_datastore_credentials (main.py:608) and load_from_db (UserSession constructor) which uses _legacy_get_all_datastore_credentials returning [].

Fix: route handlers in main.py call services.state.save_datastore_credentials / delete_datastore_credentials / list_all_datastore_credentials directly via Depends(get_db), then refresh the in-memory UserSession cache from the resulting row. Same shape as awsk-26h.2 conversions (UserRepository, DatastoreCredentialsRepository for read-only paths) but extended to include the encrypt-on-write path.

Also surface during awsk-3r4.5 smoke if not fixed first.

title: Bug: worker.import_job raises RuntimeError mid-flow — no production import job has actually run on this branch
description:
services/worker.py:93-96 short-circuits with RuntimeError("awsk-opc: get_datastore_credentials / get_setting pending repo conversion") before _import_job_body is reached. The whole import path is dead in production: queue accepts jobs, ARQ picks them up, this stub immediately marks them failed.

awsk-26h.4 already converted state.get_datastore_credentials to async repos and verified it returns decrypted access/secret keys + filespace_id + bucket_name in a dict. _import_job_body's signature already takes those fields — just needs wiring + a fix to the buggy 'll_client.configure(token="", ...)' call inside the body that resets the token to empty.

Also blocks awsk-3r4.1 (full E2E import); without this, the smoke deploys cleanly but no actual import succeeds.

title: Bug: app reads VALKEY_HOST/VALKEY_PORT but Terraform injects VALKEY_URL — prod broken
description:
Found during awsk-3r4.6 cross-cutting audit. terraform/main.tf:68 sets VALKEY_URL (rediss://default:<token>@<host>:6379 from Secrets Manager) on web/worker tasks, but every consumer in app/ reads VALKEY_HOST + VALKEY_PORT directly, ignoring VALKEY_URL. Production tasks will default to localhost:6379 (no TLS, no AUTH) and ElastiCache will reject because transit-encryption requires TLS + AUTH token.

Affected files:
- app/services/worker.py:31-32
- app/services/job_queue.py:30-31, 63-64
- app/services/metrics.py:140-141

Fix: parse VALKEY_URL in a single helper (e.g. services/valkey.py: parse_valkey_settings()) returning host/port/password/ssl, and have ARQ workers + redis clients call it. Keep VALKEY_HOST/VALKEY_PORT as a local-dev fallback when VALKEY_URL is not set (ministack runs Valkey plaintext per CLAUDE.md). Confirm worker startup against ministack still passes.

title: Operator: add AWS_ROLE_ARN to GitHub repo secrets after terraform apply
description:
Operator action — required ONLY when terraform.tfvars sets github_repo to a non-empty value (Path A: GitHub-Actions-driven CD). Operators on Path B (manual / own-CI) skip this bead entirely; the github-oidc module no-ops and there's no role ARN to push.

For Path A operators:

After 'terraform apply' lands clean (or the bootstrap TUI's apply step succeeds), publish the GitHub Actions deploy role ARN into your fork's repo secrets so .github/workflows/aws-fargate.yml can OIDC-assume it.

Concrete steps (substitute YOUR fork — the bead does NOT hardcode the upstream repo):

1. Read the role ARN from terraform outputs:
     cd terraform
     terraform output -raw github_actions_role_arn

   Returns null when var.github_repo is empty in tfvars (Path B —
   no OIDC role created in that case, this bead doesn't apply).

2. Resolve the repo path the OIDC trust policy was scoped to:
     REPO="$(grep '^github_repo' terraform/terraform.tfvars | cut -d'"' -f2)"
   Or just read it from your tfvars manually — should match the value
   you set under github_repo.

3. Push the secret with your gh auth (NOT the upstream repo's):
     gh secret set AWS_ROLE_ARN \
       --repo "$REPO" \
       --body "$(cd terraform && terraform output -raw github_actions_role_arn)"

   Or via the GitHub UI: <fork> repo Settings → Secrets and variables →
   Actions → New repository secret → Name: AWS_ROLE_ARN, Value: <arn>.

4. Verify:
     gh secret list --repo "$REPO" | grep AWS_ROLE_ARN

   Then push a no-op commit (or trigger workflow_dispatch) to confirm
   the lint-test → build-images → deploy chain in
   .github/workflows/aws-fargate.yml runs without 'AccessDenied'.

Until this is done, every PR and push to your fork's aws-fargate branch
fails at the 'aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials' step (it needs the
role ARN to assume). Lint-test stages still run because they don't need
AWS.

title: Worktree branch seeding bug: agents sometimes branch from main, not aws-kubernetes
description:
Two app-agent runs (awsk-rp6.8 and awsk-ux9.1) reported the same issue: the Agent tool's isolation:'worktree' option created the worktree branch from a non-aws-kubernetes commit (rp6.8 reset manually; ux9.1 didn't notice and ended up with a parent on the multi-user branch — its commit had to be cherry-picked rather than merged).

This is a Claude Code runtime issue, not a project bug, but worth tracking until we understand the trigger. Possible causes: agent invocation while a different branch is checked out somewhere on the host, or worktree base resolution falling back to default branch.

WORKAROUND: Always cherry-pick agent commits rather than fast-forward merging. Cherry-pick applies just the patch and ignores the (possibly wrong) base.

ACCEPTANCE: documented in CLAUDE.md as a known issue with the recommended cherry-pick workflow, OR root cause identified and fixed upstream.

description:

Scope (aws-fargate posture):
- Pre-conditions: postgres + valkey reachable (the same testcontainers fixture used by tests/db/repositories/*.py works here).
- Flow: register a user → login → POST /api/load-filespaces → POST /api/datastores/{id}/credentials → POST /api/jobs (queue an import) → assert the import_jobs row reached status='pending' and a Valkey ARQ job was enqueued.
- The actual worker pickup + LucidLink call lives in services.worker.import_job; it has its own integration test in tests/services/test_worker_idempotency_integration.py. This test stops at 'job queued', verifies the row + queue, and trusts the worker test for the back half.

Original AC referenced kind + helm + Playwright + ministack S3 + the 'lucidlink-api received the import call' assertion — all kubernetes-era. The aws-fargate translation: the lucidlink-api lives in the same Fargate task as web (sidecar), so its receipt is observable via the worker test, not the e2e test. Playwright is overkill for an HTMX server-rendered app — httpx + asserting the rendered HTML is sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
1. tests/e2e/test_full_import_flow.py exists and runs in <2 min against the testcontainers Postgres + Valkey fixture (much under the original 8-min budget — the in-process ASGI transport eliminates network round-trips).

2. Test asserts:
   a. POST /api/auth/register returns 200 + sets the access_token cookie.
   b. POST /api/load-filespaces with a mocked LucidLinkClient returns 200 and writes api_host into user_settings.
   c. POST /api/datastores/{id}/credentials with a mocked S3Service.head_bucket returns 200 and writes a row into datastore_credentials (Fernet ciphertext, decryptable via state.get_datastore_credentials).
   d. POST /api/jobs queues an import and writes a row into import_jobs with status='pending'; the ARQ Redis queue 'arq:queue' has the job enqueued.

3. Test runs cleanly under PYTEST_FAST=1 by skipping (it requires the postgres_container fixture, same as the rest of the integration suite).
